walkthroughs.body_html:
Infant baptism (Catholic, CofE, Orthodox) welcomes a child into the Church with parents/godparents promising faith.

Believer's baptism (Baptists, Pentecostals) is for those old enough to choose, by full immersion (like Jesus in the Jordan, Mark 1:9).

Water symbolises cleansing and new life.

The Eucharist remembers the Last Supper (Luke 22:19 — 'Do this in remembrance of me').

Catholics believe in transubstantiation — bread/wine truly become Jesus' body and blood.

Lutherans hold consubstantiation; many Protestants see it as symbolic memorial (Zwingli).

Quakers and the Salvation Army don't celebrate Eucharist at all.

Major Christian pilgrimage sites: Jerusalem (places of Jesus' life), Lourdes (Mary's apparitions, 1858), Iona (early Celtic Christianity), Walsingham, Rome, Santiago de Compostela.

Christmas celebrates Jesus' birth; Easter celebrates the resurrection. Lent is the 40 days of preparation before Easter.

mcqs.q: Which year did Mary appear at Lourdes?
Why do Jews not accept Jesus as the Messiah?
options: Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.
Because Jews believe Jesus never existed.
Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
Because the Jewish Messiah is expected to bring peace, rebuild the Temple and restore Israel — events the Jewish tradition holds Jesus did not accomplish.

mcqs.q: What does natural law theory base morality on?
options: Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
Natural law means whatever happens in nature is morally right.
Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.
Human nature and reason — there are objective purposes (telos) built into humans which reason can discover, generating universal moral precepts.
